{{Quote|Ah, if only you could. But the malfunction is hidden within your skull, a difficult place to make repairs. I don't know if you've seen any brains lately, but they're hard to sort out. A CPU makes more sense.|8t88|<ref name="Rebel Agent" />}}
'''8t88''' was a [[Model 88-series administration droid|Model 88]] [[Tiss'shar/Legends|Tiss'shar]] administrative [[Droid/Legends|droid]] who went rogue and became an [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]] around the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. In charge of maintaining an important [[Woostri HoloScan Database|holoscan database]] on [[Woostri/Legends|Woostri]], 88 was the recipient of an elaborate practical joke which left him with an undersized head and a bitter resentment of everything [[Human/Legends|Human]]. He became an informant on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], hoping to someday enact his revenge on those responsible for his disfigurement and built up a sizable fortune working for any and every faction in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] willing to pay his steep fees.

Shortly after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], 8t88 took a job helping a [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] named [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] locate the [[Valley of the Jedi]], which brought him into conflict with [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] agent [[Kyle Katarn]]. After narrowly escaping from Katarn on Nar Shaddaa and [[Sulon/Legends|Sulon]], the droid managed to decipher a [[Map to the Valley of the Jedi|coded map giving the coordinates of the valley]] and presented it to Jerec. The Dark Jedi instructed 8t88 to collect his payment on a freighter named the ''[[Sulon Star]]'', though in truth 88 was sent straight into an ambush and was decapitated by two of Jerec's [[Seven Dark Jedi|minions]]. Both his head and body continued to exist, albeit independently, and he eventually found vengeance on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mawan/Legends|Mawan]], where he slew the [[Zokor Polpot|perpetrator]] of the prank that left him traumatized all those years previously.

==Biography==
===Early existence===
{{Quote|When someone desires information, they come to me.|8t88|audio=TheyComeToMe-JKDFII.flac|<ref name="Dark Forces" />}}
[[File:8t88_4.jpg|thumb|left|200px|8t88 and his pet, [[Grendel]], in Barons Hed.]]
8t88 was a [[Model 88-series administration droid]]<ref name="Scavenger's Guide" /> constructed [[195 BBY|approximately 190 years]] [[Galactic Standard Calendar|before the Battle of Yavin]]<ref name="Wizards" /> by [[Uhr-Vah-Vo TechWorks]],<ref name="Scavenger's Guide" /> a [[Tiss'shar/Legends|Tiss'shar]] manufacturing company. A member of the 88 line, he was designed for bookkeeping and other administrative tasks and was eventually assigned as the leading [[Droid/Legends|droid]] in the management of the famous [[Woostri HoloScan Database|HoloScan Database]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Woostri/Legends|Woostri]]. During a visit to Woostri by several leading members of the [[University of Coruscant/Legends|University of Coruscant]], the University's Vice-Chancellor, a man named [[Zokor Polpot]], had 8t88's reptilian cranium replaced with that of a [[JMM assassin droid|JMM]] espionage droid in a prank intended to embarrass the Chancellor of the university. The event forced the Chancellor to resign, and 8t88 was left extremely traumatized. Having access only to his auxiliary hard drive's recollection of events, his memory of the perpetrators was imperfect, and lacked considerable consistency. He began to suffer from the droid equivalent of dementia, and his former intelligence was replaced with a lust for revenge. He was horrified at the fact that his new head was undersized in comparison to his lanky frame, and he began to make frequent backups of his memory banks, ensuring that he would never forget his desire for vengeance. Seeing what had happened as a sign of anti-droid prejudice, he began to hate all living beings, particularly [[Human/Legends|Humans]], and his obsession for finding the beings who had caused his disfigurement knew no end.<ref name="Wizards" />

His thirst for revenge, however, was never forgotten or diminished and when the 88 line was scrapped to make way for more modern administrative droids, 8t88 went rogue, becoming an [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]]. He figured that the abilities he retained as an accountant would prove useful in this line of work and that it would eventually provide him with leads on those responsible for his mismatched head. He also knew that acquiring as much money as he possibly could would give him an extra advantage and before long he had accumulated a staggering amount of wealth. When 8t88 found another 88 droid with its cranium tampered with, his desire for revenge was further intensified;<ref name="Wizards" /> he offered the droid no sympathy, however, using it for spare parts whenever he was in need of any.<ref name="Rebel Agent" />

8t88 saw organic concepts such as morality, justice, and loyalty petty, and he happily worked for the highest bidder, often backstabbing and selling out former associates. 88's expert skills at deciphering ancient languages and cracking top-secret codes made him a much sought-after infochant and during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], almost two hundred years after his creation, he worked for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]], and many fringe factions, building up a sturdy reputation as one of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] most reliable information brokers. 8t88 charged huge upfront fees, though his only other condition was that clients never ask from whom, how, or where he attained the information. He was not equipped for combat but his espionage-model head allowed him to constantly record events. Operating mostly out of [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]],<ref name="EGTD" /> 88 hired thugs whenever violence needed to be used, although the top notch [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] of the era usually steered well clear of the double-crossing droid.<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> 8t88 was said to be heartless&mdash;a metaphor he heartily endorsed&mdash;though he did care for one thing other than revenge: his pet [[hornagaunt]], a massive beast named [[Grendel]].<ref name="Wizards" /> 8t88's contemptuous nature did not win him any favors among his clientèle, who found his attitude and expensive fees annoying. Few customers stayed with 88 for long, though he did not care, as there were always people in need of his services on Nar Shaddaa.<ref name="FF">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 121|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 121]]</ref>

===Working for Jerec===
{{Quote|I should have aimed for your head when I had the chance.''"<br />"''A lost opportunity.|Kyle Katarn and 8t88|audio=LostOpportunity-JKDFII.flac|<ref name="Dark Forces" />}}[[File:Katarn_meets_8t88.jpg|thumb|left|8t88 giving information to Katarn, before the agent was jumped by his thugs.]]
In [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], 8t88 outbid an [[Assembler]] information broker named [[Balancesheet]] to assist the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] in locating the elusive [[Valley of the Jedi]].<ref name="Wizards" /> His search led him to the world of [[Sulon/Legends|Sulon]] and the abandoned [[Katarn estate]], which was the former residence of Rebel leader [[Morgan Katarn]], executed by Jerec himself several years earlier. There 88 salvaged several [[Hologram disc/Legends|holodiscs]] but despite his aptitute with codes, he was unable to decipher one, to his immense frustration. Knowing it was likely of great importance, the droid arranged a meeting with Katarn's son, [[Kyle Katarn]], who was seeking knowledge on the identity of his father's killer, at the [[Rimmer's Rest/Legends|Rimmer's Rest]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] on Nar Shaddaa. 88 went to the meeting place an hour before Katarn was due to arrive, hoping to recruit the bounty hunter [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] to act as a bodyguard, in case Katarn refused to assist the droid in cracking the holodisc's code. However the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] (who had [[Mission to Coruscant (Kyle Katarn)|met]] Katarn earlier<ref name="Star Wars: Dark Forces">''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]''</ref>) knowing his [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] affiliation, and that the Alliance would eventually [[New Republic/Legends|come to the top]], refused the job. The information broker was disappointed at being unable to acquire Fett's services (who made sure before parting to point out the droid's squeaking joints) and made do with [[Unidentified Gran (Rimmer's Rest)|several]] [[Unidentified bounty hunter (Rimmer's Rest)|other]] [[Alien/Legends|alien]] thugs instead.<ref name="Rebel Agent" />

88 met with Katarn, as he was re-playing a [[Hologram/Legends|holo]] of his father in a booth, making a sarcasting comment for the biological having to relive an emotional moment. As the droid started giving the information Katarn wanted, the agent kept holding his [[Bryar pistol/Legends|Bryar pistol]] near its head, until it slowly revealed that the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] Jerec was his father's killer; the sound of the vaguely familiar name shocked Katarn whose thoughts were cut short finding himself surrounded by hired thugs. The droid offered Kyle his life in exchange for decoding his father's holodisc but the Rebel agent refused to cooperate. 8t88 ordered the man's death and left.<ref name="Dark Forces" />

[[File:8t88_3.jpg|thumb|150px|8t88 flees from Kyle Katarn.]]
The Tiss'shar droid formulated various lies to tell Jerec to account for his failure as he ran to a landing pad on the moon, where [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|''Lambda''-class shuttle]] ''[[Furious (Lambda-class)|Furious]]'' was due to collect him. Katarn, however, not only managed to incapacitate the droid's mercenaries, but had placed a [[tracker droid]] on the informant's leg, and gave chase; the tracker was only discovered and destroyed by [[Grentho]], but it was too late as Katarn catched up with them to the [[Launch Platform Three]], just as 8t88 was about to board the shuttle, congratulating [[Unidentified pilot (Furious)|its pilot]] for being prompt; with a precise blaster shot, he blew off one of the infochant's arms. The arm, along with the holodisc it held, fell down into the bowels of the Smuggler's Moon, thirty stories below. 88's guards distracted Katarn while the droid jumped onto the shuttle while Jerec's Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] made sure they didn't follow it inside. The shuttle set off while a [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa bomber]] picked up the pieces, and the droid traveled back to Sulon.<ref name="Rebel Agent" />

===Dignitary in the Dark Palace===
[[File:8t88s_shuttle.png|thumb|left|250px|Jerec's ''Lambda''-class [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]], [[Furious (Lambda-class)|''Furious'']].]]
Jerec's [[Seven Dark Jedi|minions]] had found the [[map to the Valley of the Jedi]] on the ceiling of Morgan Katarn's home during the events on Nar Shaddaa; they removed the ceiling panels and had them brought to [[Barons Hed]], the moon's capital city. 88's shuttle brought him back to Sulon, and the [[Government House (Sulon)|Government House]] of [[Barons Hed]] that once served as Jerec's palace, where he enjoyed the service of [[Unidentified majordomo (Jerec)|Jerec's majordomo]]. Fed up with the droid's attitude, the majordomo assigned to him a dreary room without windows adjacent to the ballroom as a humiliating jest. 8t88 took pleasure in the fact that all of those who had been assigned to protect him at Barons Hed, were organics&mdash;a reverse on the usual occurrence of droids serving Humans that he was so contemptuous of. An arm was transported there from the other, obsolete 88 unit that existed solely for being salvaged for its spare parts, and 88 did the job of a [[roboticist]] by refitting himself with it. He didn't miss the oportunity to bully [[Rol (Human)|one of his henchmen]] for failing to provide the correct tools.<ref name="Rebel Agent" />

Before anything else he decided to take Jerec's majordomo to task for the "guest quarters" assigned to him and sought explanations from the "fool in charge" for the room's purpose; the man didn't expect that the droid would ever notice it, and after bluffing that it was practical for his work and pet, later begged for mercy and offered to make amends. The droid knew that biological brains are unfixable, and simply removed it from the man's head, feeding his body to Grendel.<ref name="Rebel Agent" /><ref name="RAAD">[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent (audio drama)|''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' audio drama]]</ref>

Making an example of the majordomo, the staff became more servile and assigned him to a more luxurious room with a throne. After considerable effort, the Map pieces transferred there by the Dark Jed were reassembled on a table and the droid managed to decipher it and create a digital reconstruction. The digital copy of it and stored the location of the valley in his memory banks. With the map entirely decoded, 8t88 contacted Jerec on his [[Vengeance (Vengeance-class)|flagship]] and sent him the coordinates of [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]] as a [[Holomap/Legends|holomap]]. The [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]] expressed his thanks before informing 88 that he would receive his payment on one of Jerec's ships, the ''[[Sulon Star]]'', in a [[Fuel City|refueling station]] outside of Barons Hed.<ref name="Rebel Agent" />

Unbeknown to 8t88, Katarn had survived and tracked him to Barons Hed. The Rebel infiltrated 88's building, slaying the droids various bodyguards. He and 8t88 faced off, with Katarn demanding that the Tiss'shar droid hand over the map. Before things developed, however, Jerec's Dark Jedi, [[Yun]], attacked Kyle, giving 8t88 the opportunity to flee.<ref name="Rebel Agent" />

===Double cross on the ''Sulon Star''===
{{Quote|I'm here for my well deserved payment!|8t88, to Pic, moments before his deactivation|audio=WellDeservedPayment-JKDFII.flac|<ref name="Dark Forces" />}}
[[File:WeeGee.jpg|thumb|[[WeeGee]] activates 8t88's head to project his memorized holomap.]]
While Yun was dealing with Katarn, 8t88 and Grendel made off toward the Fuel City in a shuttle; they arrived at the ''Sulon Star'' and 88 allowed Grendel to come with him, in lieu of a bodyguard.<ref name="Rebel Agent" /><ref name="RAAD" /> They met with two more of Jerec's darksiders, the unlikely duo of [[Picaroon C. Boodle|Pic]] and [[Gorc]]; the presence of the two [[Brothers of the Sith]] unsettled 8t88, who thought it unlikely that Jerec would send two of his best underlings on a simple payment mission. He knew something was amiss but demanded his payment anyway. 8t88 had outlived his use for Jerec, and the man ordered his Dark Jedi to destroy the droid; they [[Sai cha/Legends|decapitated]] him.<ref name="Rebel Agent" /><ref name="Dark Forces" />

The two Dark Jedi placed 8t88's head precariously atop his shoulders and left him in a compartment; in the dim lighting he appeared to be operational. When Kyle Katarn arrived on the ship, he thought he had been triumphant in his chase for the droid, though 88's cranium soon clattered to the floor.<ref name="Dark Forces" /><ref name="Rebel Agent" /><ref name="RAAD" /> Then Gorc emerged and taunting Kyle, he fed the droid's head to Grendel,<ref name="RAAD" /> who swallowed his master's head; Katarn slew Gorc and dueled with Pic, temporarily incapacitating the [[Kowakian monkey-lizard/Legends|Kowakian monkey-lizard]], then killed Grendel and used [[Qu Rahn's lightsaber|his lightsaber]] to carve open one of the hornagaunt's stomachs and retrieve the severed head. Katarn ended the battle soon after, using 8t88's head to bash Pic's skull; in an ironic twist, 8t88 had exacted revenge on his deactivator.<ref name="Rebel Agent" /><ref name="RAAD" />

Katarn escaped the planet with 8t88's remains, and used his own family droid [[WeeGee]] to download the [[Holomap/Legends|holomap]] of the Valley of the Jedi from it.<ref name="Dark Forces" />

===Second reactivation===
{{Quote|This looks familiar.|[[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]]|<ref name="Mysteries of the Sith">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Mysteries of the Sith]]''</ref>}}
8t88 was believed to have been deactivated, but several years later [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] came across 88's head on [[Rathalay]], in [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] kingpin [[Kaerobani]]'s [[Kaerobani's base|lair]],<ref name="Mysteries of the Sith" /> bitterly plotting to reclaim his lost body. While his head was never known to have left Rathalay, 8t88's body may well have continued to exist after the events on the ''Sulon Star''. Reports from all corners of the galaxy indicated that an 88 droid sporting a variety of cranium units was running amok. One of the heads was that of a [[Phase I Dark Trooper|Phase I]] [[Dark Trooper/Legends|dark trooper]] sighted on the planet [[Neshtab]]; another was utilizing a [[BL-series Battle Legionnaire|BL series droid]] head on the planet [[Keyorin]] in the [[Belderone system/Legends|Belderone system]], while he next resurfaced with an [[ASP-series labor droid/Legends|ASP-series droid's]] head on ''[[Omze's Incredible Traveling Starport/Legends|Omze's Incredible Traveling Starport]]''. The ASP cranium had extremely limited vocabulary, which caused 8t88 immense frustration.<ref name="Wizards" /> Truly missing his cranial unit, the droid was willing to pay a handsome sum of money for an 88-series head, while also intent on using an 88-series body for spare parts should he find one. However, Model 88-series droids&mdash;especially those with their original heads still intact&mdash;had become a rare sight in the galaxy, as most of them had been scrapped after the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="Scavenger's Guide" /> As 8t88 was among the last of his kind, there was little doubt among the [[New Republic Intelligence Service]] that the sightings were of his body.<ref name="Wizards" />

8t88 eventually found his vengeance. The latest sighting of the mysterious 88 droid was on the planet [[Mawan/Legends|Mawan]], where it was spotted with a head similar to that of an [[EV-series supervisor droid/Legends|EV-series supervisor droid's]] robotic skull. The sighting coincided with a tragic and fatal accident suffered by visiting University of Coruscant Chancellor Zokor Polpot. Realizing that 8t88 was a threat not to be ignored, New Republic Intelligence [[General/Legends|General]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]] created individual entries for both 8t88's head and torso in his [[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|Most Wanted List]].<ref name="Wizards" />

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|But I'm not without a heart.|8t88, to Kyle Katarn|audio=NotWOAHeart-JKDFII.flac|<ref name="Rebel Agent" />}}[[File:8t88_egtd.png|thumb|right|250px|8t88 [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]].]]
After his ordeal on Woostri, 88 became extremely contemptuous of all living beings and vowed never again to serve organics. He never did, unless he was calling the shots himself.<ref name="Wizards" /> The thought that he was created by biologicals, and that now biologicals often would serve him as hirelings or servants, was pleasing to him and didn't miss a chance bullying them around or punishing them.<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> 88 found the very idea of breathing disgusting, and thought that CPUs made far more sense than biological organs. He did, however, have many Human-like emotions, and somehow possessed the ability to instinctively know when something was amiss; what many called "a [[I have a bad feeling about this|bad feeling]]."<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> Because he had not had a memory wipe in over a decade, during the Valley of the Jedi incident, 8t88 may not have been entirely mentally sound; he suffered from the robotic equivalent of dementia and his lust for revenge and hatred of Humans often clouded his judgment.<ref name="Wizards" />

A selfish criminal,<ref name="Scavenger's Guide" /> 8t88 cared little for other beings, be they droids or organics. He maintained a fellow 88 unit simply for salvaging it for spare parts, not caring at all about its feelings or thoughts on slowly being reduced to nothing. 88, although he often got himself into situations which called for violence, never got his hands dirty, preferring to have other, expendable cutthroats carry out deeds for him.<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> 8t88 also saw himself as above the concepts of loyalty, justice, and morality, and had great disdain for them.<ref name="EGTD" />

==Features==
{{Quote|I can decipher any language or code known, but this one eludes me.|8t88|audio=ThisOneEludesMe-JKDFII.flac|<ref name="Dark Forces" />}}
8t88's skeleton-body was silver and powered by hydraulic tubing, which caused his movements to make a great deal of noise. In addition, a tapping noise constantly issued from his interior.<ref name="Dark Forces" /> Later in his existence, 88's noisy joints were often in need of oiling,<ref name="EGTD" /> a fact that many, including bounty hunter Boba Fett, used to taunt and mock him.<ref name="Rebel Agent" /> 8t88 had two thin limbs, which were quite fragile and susceptible to damage<ref name="Dark Forces" /><ref name="Rebel Agent" /> and large Tiss'shar talons for hands.<ref name="EGTD" />

8t88 was possessed of a variety of functions, afforded to him by both his original design<ref name="EGTD" /> and his JMM droid head.<ref name="Wizards" /><ref name="EGTD" /> He had a number of communication devices built into his frame, and his specially-modified [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]] spoke in an intelligent, elegant, well-mannered voice. He also had several special storage compartments in his frame, as he wore no clothes. He was also equipped with an infrared sensor, a microscopic imager, a [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] projector/recorder, extremely perceptive audio sensors, a concealed beam transmitter, and a broadband communication antenna, as well as a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]], heuristic processor, improved sensor package, and translator unit.<ref name="Wizards" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Years ago, I was planning to write a NJO-era short story for ''Star Wars Gamer'' starring Grand Admiral Grant and 8t88, in which Grant broke his "comfortable retirement on Rathalay" in order to fight off an invading Yuuzhan Vong warrior. 8t88's head played a supporting role! Unfortunately I didn't sell the story on my first attempt, and a short time later ''Star Wars Gamer'' went under.|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="Wallace">{{JCFCite|url=posts/24396345|board=Literature|thread=New Essential Guide to Droids|user=Dan Wallace|date=2006-07-17|time=2:36 pm|archivedate=20180317235712}}</ref>}}
Created by [[Justin Chin]], 8t88 debuted in the PC game ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]'' in the year [[1997]], where he acted as one of several main villains, albeit the only one which the players did not have to defeat themselves. His disembodied head has a cameo appearance in ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Mysteries of the Sith]]''. 8t88's backstory was left largely undeveloped in ''Dark Forces II'', though ''[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent]]'', one of three novellas retelling the story of the game, featured several chapters written from 8t88's point of view, providing some of his backstory. ''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]'', ''[[The Dark Forces Saga]]'' and ''[[Kyle Katarn's Tale]]'' further developed his backstory, with the ''Essential Guide'' containing schematics of the droid.

[[Daniel Wallace]] has said that he planned to write a short-story starring the retired [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Octavian Grant]] and 8t88's head set during the [[New Jedi Order era]] for the ''[[Star Wars]] [[Star Wars Gamer|Gamer]]'' magazine. In the story, Grant&mdash;the very kind of anti-droid being that 88 detested&mdash;teamed up with the droid's head to fend off a [[Yuuzhan Vong]] warrior on Rathalay during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]. The story never materialized, and ''Gamer'' was canceled shortly afterward.<ref name="Wallace" />

8t88 was voiced by [[Denny Delk]] in the cutscenes of ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]'' and [[Peter Moore]] in [[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent (audio drama)|''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' audio drama]].
